processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots were prepared in a vacuum induction furnace.
Hot-rolled to a thickness of ~3 mm.
Cold-rolled to a final thickness of around 1.5 mm.
Water quenching to room temperature; intended to produce ultrafine γ+α aggregate and δ-ferrite.

processing_steps.method: uniaxial tensile loading along rolling direction (parallel to the banding direction)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Tensile loading axis is parallel to the rolling direction (parallel to the banding direction).

structures.overall_structure: Banded/layered structure composed of ultrafine-grained γ+α aggregates (reversely transformed from martensite during annealing) and coarse-grained δ-ferrite; the band direction is along RD.

phases_present.morphology: coarse-grained, banded along RD; retained from hot rolling and recrystallized/grown during intercritical annealing
phases_present.texture: {100}<011> rotated cube texture; <011>//RD and {100}//ND; maximum intensity 2.57

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: coarse grains, above ~15 μm; histogram spanning ~5–55 μm with peak near 37 μm

phases_present.morphology: ultrafine-grained, reversely transformed from martensite during annealing

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: ultrafine grains (as small as ~1 μm); γ histogram peaks near 1.8 μm, α below ~5 μm

defect_interactions.interaction_type: GND accumulation and strain concentration at δ-ferrite/UFG γ+α phase boundary
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Strain localises preferentially at the δ-ferrite/UFG γ+α phase boundary; a high density of GNDs is produced to accommodate the hardness/stiffness difference between the two constituents under iso-strain condition.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Strain-induced α'-martensite formation (TRIP effect) makes a major contribution to strain-hardening; martensite nucleates primarily at austenite/ferrite (α or δ) phase boundaries; the RD sample shows faster martensite transformation kinetics than the TD sample.
interfaces.interface_notes: In the RD sample the δ-ferrite and UFG γ+α aggregates deform to a similar level (iso-strain condition), with strain concentration still observed at the phase boundary between them.

measurement_conditions.environment: quasi-static uniaxial tension (in-situ HEXRD tensile stage)
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: HEXRD tensile gauge length 12 mm, width 2 mm, thickness 1.2 mm; μ-DIC dog-bone gauge length 20 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the RD oriented sample (red curve) is shown in Fig. 4(a); the RD curve reaches higher stress and larger strain before fracture.

service_conditions.stress_state: uniaxial tension along RD (parallel to the banding direction)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: strain-hardening capability, tensile strength, ductility, and strain-induced martensite transformation kinetics

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss-Crossbeam 340 scanning electron microscopy (SEM); analyzed with TSL OIM and AZtecCrystal software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Samples finally polished with 0.02 μm silica suspension
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization of undeformed and interrupted tensile specimens (phase fraction, grain size)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Banded UFG γ+α + coarse δ-ferrite; austenite ~1.8 μm, α-ferrite ~2 μm, δ-ferrite ~38 μm; no martensite in non-deformed state.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Talos F200X operated at 200 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens prepared by mechanical grinding followed by twin-jet polishing using a 10 % perchloric acid methanol solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine detailed deformation behavior of interrupted tensile specimens

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Average value taken from more than five different measurements within each region; specimens prepared as for EBSD
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness at different localized regions (UFG γ+α aggregate and δ-ferrite)
characterization_methods.key_findings: UFG γ+α region 221±3.0 HV; δ-ferrite 205±1.5 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: P02.1 Powder Diffraction and Total Scattering Beamline, PETRA III, DESY; fixed energy ~60 keV, wavelength ~0.20738 Å; beam size 0.5 × 0.5 mm^2; Varex XRD 4343CT fast area detector (1 s/frame); Kammrath & Weiss stress rig
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tension, initial strain rate ~1×10^-3 s^-1; tensile gauge 12 mm × 2 mm × 1.2 mm; detector calibrated with CeO2; diffraction rings divided into 36 sectors (10° each); sector −5° to 5° used for lattice strain
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify deformation-induced phase transformation, lattice strain and dislocation density
characterization_methods.key_findings: RD sample shows faster strain-induced α'-martensite formation and higher austenite dislocation density than TD.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Kammrath & Weiss GmbH tensile stage within a Tescan Mira4 SEM; images processed with La Vision DaVis software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Dog-bone specimens with gauge length 20 mm; nano-scale gold speckles applied by gold sputtering and gold film remodeling; secondary electron imaging over 500 × 500 μm^2 at interrupted strains
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigate strain partitioning between different phases during deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: RD sample: δ-ferrite and UFG γ+α aggregates show similar deformation levels; strain concentration within γ-α' mixed phase up to 1.3 times higher than α phase; strain localises at δ/γ+α phase boundary.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: MAUD software for austenite volume fraction; Fit2D software for diffraction intensity integration
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine austenite volume fraction and integrate diffraction intensities

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: XRD line-profile analysis of five FCC reflections {111}, {200}, {220}, {311}, {222}
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: β determined by trial-and-error; β_RD = 0.002 at ε~0.14 and 0.0018 at ε~0.22
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite dislocation density higher in the RD sample (by a maximum of ~1.51 × 10^14 m^-2).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pseudo-binary equilibrium phase diagram for Fe-7.95Mn-0.25C-4.94Al (wt.%) steel; red annotation at 850 °C and ~4.94 wt.% Al shows the alloy sits in the γ+α two-phase field.

computational_details.simulation_method: Olson-Cohen (OC) model for deformation-induced martensite transformation kinetics
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: n=2 assumed (random martensite nucleation); fitting parameters obtained from TD sample are applied to RD with austenite plastic strain ε_RD = 1.15 ε_TD.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: OC model predictions compared with HEXRD experimental martensite fraction data (Fig. 14); model under-predicts at high strain.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict deformation-induced martensite fraction: F_m = F_γ0 × {1 - exp[-β[1-exp(-αε)]^n]}
analytical_models.model_note: The OC model is used to calculate RD martensite transformation kinetics from the TD behaviour; parameters α, β, n summarized in Table 1.

analytical_models.equation_role: Dislocation density from diffraction peak broadening: ΔK − βW_hkl = 0.9/L + (πA^2 b^2/2)^(1/2) ρ^(1/2) (K C̄^(1/2))
analytical_models.model_note: β_RD = 0.002 at ε~0.14 and 0.0018 at ε~0.22 (trial-and-error determination).

unmapped_findings: The intercritically annealed steel (average of RD and TD samples) demonstrates tensile strength ~855 ± 35 MPa and total elongation 65 ± 5 % (b0045).
The RD sample has a higher strength (864 MPa) and ductility (69 %) than the TD sample; RD maximum strain-hardening rate 2052 MPa vs TD 1828 MPa (b0045).
Stage II strain hardening begins at a true strain of ~0.2 for both RD and TD samples; the RD sample shows higher strain-hardening rate at stages II and III (b0045).

δ-phase texture: major rotated cube component {100}<011> with <011>//RD and {100}//ND, maximum intensity 2.57; Taylor factors 2.83 (RD) and 2.78 (TD), indicating similar δ-phase mechanical response (b0077).
At the elastic stage (true strain below ~0.03) the martensite fraction is negligible (less than 1 vol.%), indicating strain-induced α'-martensite forms primarily during plastic deformation (b0053).
The RD sample shows higher martensite transformation kinetics than TD; the difference can be as high as 4 vol. % at a true strain of ~0.48 (uniform elongation of TD) (b0053).
RD martensite fraction reaches approximately 25 % near true strain ~0.48 while TD reaches about 21 % near strain ~0.5 (figure_014).
RD austenite dislocation density is higher than TD, with the RD value approaching ~10 × 10^14 m^-2 near ~0.45 true strain (figure_009).
The volume expansion associated with the γ to α'-martensitic transformation is around 2~4 % and may contribute to local plastic strain increase in the γ-α' mixed phase (b0075).

Within the UFG γ+α region, strain in the γ-α' mixed phase is up to 1.3 times higher than in the α phase for both samples; the austenite plastic strain in RD is higher than in TD by a factor of ~1.15 (b0075, b0087).

In the RD sample, the δ-ferrite and UFG γ+α aggregates deform at similar levels (iso-strain condition), whereas the TD sample shows pronounced strain partitioning with higher strain in δ-ferrite (b0063, b0068, b0075).
Weighted average lattice strain onset of plastic deformation (RD): austenite (FCC) deviates from linearity at 1.8 % applied strain, ferrite (BCC) at 2.3 %; austenite yields first (b0081, figure_013).
β_RD (stacking fault contribution parameter) = 0.002 at true strain ~0.14 and 0.0018 at true strain ~0.22 (b0059, figure_009).
No extensometer was used in the HEXRD tensile tests; only applied tensile load and crosshead displacement were recorded (b0027).

The paper's conclusion states that RD-deformed samples exhibited higher tensile strength and ductility than TD samples due to faster strain-induced α'-martensite kinetics and higher austenite dislocation density (b0097).
